SLATE VALLEY — a long trough of wet blue-grey slate running between two steep pitches, brimming with rainwater, a row of stubby clay chimney pots standing along its near lip and a lead hopper at the low end; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of hazed spires and mill chimneys across the top; seen obliquely from the flat of the next roof at the same height, looking across the valley.

COPPER CUPOLA CLUSTER — four onion-domed copper cupolas gone brilliant verdigris, each ringed with a little iron rail, the leadwork between them worn to silver by feet; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of dark warehouse roofs and one gasholder across the top; seen from beside the nearest cupola, looking across the others.

TARRED FLAT — a broad flat roof of black tarred felt patched in overlapping squares, a lead-lined water tank up on timber trestles, a coil of hemp rope and a pile of spare slate stacked against the parapet; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of smoking terraces across the top; seen from knee height on the felt, looking across it.

RIDGE WALKWAY — a narrow plank catwalk pegged along the very ridge of a long roof with a thin iron handrail on one side only, the tiles falling steeply away on both hands, moss thick in every joint; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of church towers and rooflines across the top; seen from a step above the walkway, looking across it and across the tiles beyond.

SNOW-LOADED PANTILES — deep overlapping terracotta pantiles under a hand's depth of clean snow, the snow slumped and curling off the eaves in a frozen wave, a swept black path trodden across it; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of white roofs and black chimney stacks across the top; seen obliquely from a dormer sill, looking across the slope.

FOUNDRY-DISTRICT CRUST — low warehouse roofs under a crust of black soot an inch thick, every skylight opaque with it, one skylight wiped clean in a single arc by somebody's sleeve; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of squat brick and leaning stacks across the top; seen from the top of a short iron ladder, level with the roof.

ARCADE GLASS — the great curved glass barrel of a shopping arcade running below and beside us, its iron ribs black against the lit glass, a walkway of open grating bolted along its flank for the men who clean it; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of ornate stone frontages across the top; seen from the grating walkway, looking across the glass.

MANSARD ROW — a run of steep grey-black mansard slopes studded with small dormer windows, each dormer with its own tiny lead roof and one with its sash propped open on a stick; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of mansards and iron finials across the top; seen obliquely from a dormer top, looking across the row.

CHURCH LEADS — the broad flat lead roof of a nave, its seams rolled in long ridges, a squat stone tower shouldering up out of it on the right with a gargoyle spout jutting from its corner; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of tenement roofs across the top; seen from the leads themselves, looking across past the tower's foot.

PIGEON-LOFT ROOF — a tiled roof with a big timber pigeon loft built right onto it, its landing shelf worn pale, a washing rope strung from its corner to a chimney with three shirts on it, feathers everywhere in the gutter; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of chimneys and drying-ropes across the top; seen from beside the loft door, looking across the tiles.

GASHOLDER CROWN — the vast shallow iron drum-top of a gasholder, riveted in curved iron sheets and painted a flaking oxide red, a spiral stair coming up its outer guide-frame and a walkway round its rim; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of streets and steeples across the top; seen from the rim walkway, looking across the drum.

STEPPED WAREHOUSE ROOFS — broad slate roofs stepping down in wide stages like a flight of giant shallow treads, each step with its own parapet gutter full of standing water and one with a rusted crane jib still bolted to it; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of dock cranes across the top; seen from the topmost step, looking across and down the stages.

MARKET-HALL GLAZING — the huge glazed roof of a market hall right below us, hundreds of small panes in iron frames with green weed growing in every frame's gutter, warm light coming up faintly through the dirty glass; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of brick and wharf gables across the top; seen from a maintenance gantry above the glazing, looking across it.

CANAL-SIDE FLANKS — a low roof wedged between two tall brick flanks, the brick furred with soot and crossed by an iron ladder and a run of cables, one fern growing out of a crack in it; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of wharf roofs and a bridge across the top; seen from the low roof, looking up and across at the flank.

MIRROR-WET SLATES — new-laid slate still streaming after rain, every slate holding the sky like a black mirror, a lead gutter running full and one slate chipped white where a boot went through; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of wet roofs across the top; seen obliquely from a chimney's foot, looking across the wet slate.

DOME FLANK — the lead-clad flank of a great dome curving up out of the roof on the right and running out past the top edge of the frame, its lead seams standing proud like ribs, a narrow inspection walkway with a chain handrail bolted round its base; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of roofs and steeples across the top; seen from the walkway at the dome's foot, looking across the roof.

COLOSSAL STACK — a modest tiled roof crowded up against the base of an enormous round brick chimney that fills the right of the frame and runs out past the top edge, its iron hoop-bands wide as a cart; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of smaller stacks across the top; seen from the tiles, looking across at the stack's foot.

IRON FOOTBRIDGE — two roofs linked by a slender cast-iron footbridge with pierced lattice sides and a plank deck, the gap beneath it black, a bucket left standing in the middle of the deck; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of rooftops and one dome across the top; seen from one roof end, looking across the bridge.

HOTEL CRESTING — a grand roof of banded slate with ornate cast-iron cresting along its ridge, four tall brass cowl vents turning in a row, a neat swept walkway of concrete slabs laid across the lead; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of grand frontages across the top; seen from the walkway, looking across the cresting.

HARD FROST — a plain tiled roof furred white with hoar frost, every tile edge picked out in ice crystals, the frost broken in one dark trodden strip and a frozen puddle in the gutter; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of frosted roofs and cold chimneys across the top; seen obliquely from a low parapet, looking across the frost.

BREWERY HOODS — a roof crowded with great copper vent hoods over the mash tuns, each one streaked green and dripping, a timber duckboard path threading between them and a shovel leaned against one; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of brewery roofs and one blunt square tower across the top; seen from the duckboards, looking across the hoods.

TRESTLE TANK — a flat roof dominated by a huge riveted iron water tank up on timber trestles, its underside dripping, a ladder pegged up its side and a nest of pipes going down through the roof; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of tenements across the top; seen from beneath the trestles, looking out and across.

MAIN ON SADDLES — a long flat roof carrying a great iron water main across it on cast saddles, the main as thick as a barrel and weeping at every joint, green stain running away from each weep; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of roofs and a viaduct across the top; seen from beside a saddle, looking across the main.

TENEMENT PATCHWORK — a poor roof mended a hundred times in mismatched slate, tin and tar, a broken skylight boarded with a door, somebody's chair sat out on the flat part; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of crowded roofs across the top; seen from the flat part, looking across the patchwork.

LEAD FLATS AND CISTERN — worn lead flats behind a stone parapet, an open stone cistern in the middle of them half full of black water with a lily pad in it, the parapet capped in flat stones with grass in the joints; the roof plane crosses the picture from the left edge to the right edge and both ends run out of frame, the far city a low band of stone parapets and finials across the top; seen from the parapet corner, looking across the flats.
